declarations.description:
Attaches related buttons into one control: shared borders, outside corners only, a divider between items. Children
are `c2-button` or `c2-icon-button` elements (any element works for layout). With `selection="single"` the group is
a segmented control that keeps one item pressed; with `selection="multiple"` each item toggles independently. Set
`orientation="vertical"` to stack either appearance and use Up/Down keyboard navigation. The
pressed items carry `selected` (and `aria-pressed`), the group reports them in `value` and fires `input` and `change`.

A single-selection group is one Tab stop, like a radio group: Tab lands on the pressed item and the arrow keys move
the selection. Set `toolbar` for a toolbar: the group takes the `toolbar` role and stays one Tab stop, and the arrow
keys, Home and End move focus across every focusable child (buttons, `c2-select`, `c2-text-field`, links) without
changing the selection, which Space and Enter still do. A key the focused control uses itself — a caret moving in a
text field, a select opening — is left to it.

With a `name`, the group is a form control: it submits its pressed values under that name (one entry per value
with `selection="multiple"`), resets with its form and follows a disabled `<fieldset>`.
declarations.name: ButtonGroup

cssProperties.description: Space between items. Zero attaches them; a positive gap separates them into individually rounded buttons.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group--gap

cssProperties.description: Outside corner radius. With a positive gap, applies to every item.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group--border-radius

cssProperties.description: Border applied to every item, e.g. `1px solid #d4d4d8` for an outlined group.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group--border

cssProperties.description: Width of the line between attached items; also how much their borders overlap.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group__divider--width

cssProperties.description: Colour of the line between attached items. Match the border colour for outlined groups, `transparent` for none.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group__divider--color

cssProperties.description: `1 1 0` makes every item grow to the same width.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group__item--flex

cssProperties.description: Track background in the segmented appearance.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group__segmented--background-color

cssProperties.description: Track border in the segmented appearance.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group__segmented--border

cssProperties.description: Sliding selection indicator animation duration. In the segmented appearance the group owns its children's surface variables with an important cascade layer. Theme the control through the `segmented-*` and `indicator-*` variables above; app-wide `c2-button` defaults will not leak into the segmented surface.
cssProperties.name: --c2-button-group__indicator--transition-duration

members.name: selection
members.description: `none` (default) for plain attached buttons, `single` for one pressed item, `multiple` for independent toggles.

members.name: value
members.description: `value` of the pressed item; comma-separated values with `selection="multiple"`. Items without a `value` attribute use their index.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Disables every item.

members.name: orientation
members.description: Stacks the items vertically.

members.name: appearance
members.description: `segmented` adds an inset track and sliding selected surface and always uses single selection.

members.name: size
members.description: Segmented control size.

members.name: toolbar
members.description:
Makes the group a toolbar: the `toolbar` role, one Tab stop, and arrow-key focus across every focusable child,
which may be any control rather than only buttons.

members.name: name
members.description: Name the pressed values are submitted under. Without one the group takes no part in a form.

members.name: stretched
members.description: Makes the group and every item share the available width.

members.name: ariaLabel
members.description: Accessible name of the group.

members.name: activeItem
members.description: The item that holds the group's Tab stop in a toolbar: the one focused last.

members.name: defaultValue
members.description: `value` as the page first set it, restored by a form reset.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: Disabled by an ancestor `<fieldset>`, which the group treats like its own `disabled`.

members.name: items
members.description: The item elements, in order.

members.name: selectedValues
members.description: Values of the pressed items.

members.name: formResetCallback
members.description: Form reset: back to the value the page started with.

members.name: formDisabledCallback
members.description: A disabled `<fieldset>` disables the group exactly like its own `disabled`.

members.name: syncFormValue
members.description: What the form submits: nothing without a name, one entry per pressed value otherwise.

members.name: syncItems
members.description: Mirrors `value`, `selection` and `disabled` onto the items.

members.name: roving
members.description: Whether the group is one Tab stop whose position it manages: a toolbar, or a single-selection group.

members.name: focusableItems
members.description: Items the arrow keys can reach: enabled and focusable, in order.

members.name: syncTabStops
members.description:
Keeps exactly one item in the Tab order while roving: the last focused item in a toolbar, otherwise the pressed
one, falling back to the first. The others get `tabindex="-1"`, which takes a host's whole shadow tree out of the
Tab order; the current one keeps the author's own `tabindex`, which is remembered and put back when roving stops.
(Giving it `tabindex="0"` instead would make a host that forwards `focus()` a Tab stop of its own.)

members.name: itemOf
members.description: The direct child that contains the event's target, if any.

members.name: commit
members.description: Sets the selection the way a user does: `value`, then `input` and `change`.

events.name: input
events.description: Fired just before `change`, for two-way bindings that listen for `input`. Not fired for programmatic changes.

events.name: change
events.description: Fired after the user changes the selection. `detail.value` is the new `value`. Not fired for programmatic changes.
